q: Advance Ruling will be binding: i) on the applicant who had sought it in respect of any matter referred to in sub-section (2) of section 97 of CGST Act for advance ruling; (b) on the concerned officer or the jurisdictional officer in respect of the applicant:
e: TRUE — that is the right answer. The statement is (A) TRUE. An advance ruling binds the applicant who sought it — on the matters referred under Section 97(2) — and also binds the concerned or jurisdictional officer in respect of that applicant. It does not operate as a general precedent for other taxpayers; its binding force is limited to the applicant and his assessing officer. Notice how precisely the correct option is worded. The paper tests exact scope here, not an approximate idea, which is why careful reading of the question stem matters.

e: A clear grasp of the concept makes this question straightforward. The statement is (A) TRUE. ITC on partially-eligible (C2) expenditure is worked out by the proportion of Total Taxable Supplies divided by Total Supplies (taxable supplies plus exempt supplies), so that the credit attributable to exempt supplies is reversed. e: The correct answer is TRUE. The statement is (A) TRUE. In the Railways the anti-profiteering rule finds application through the GST neutralisation policy and in the finalisation of tenders when GST rates keep changing — so that rate reductions or ITC gains flow to the Railways as the recipient rather than being retained by the contractor.
